title: Lapland: 5.2 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €211,500 a year
markdown:
# Lapland: 5.2 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €211,500 a year

> Closes 5.2 of 12.1 missing patients a year (43%) · €211,500 of €2.00M · €1.79M left: nothing else pays off at these assumptions

## The gap

Of 100 lung cancer patients in Lapland, 18 get treatment that aims to cure. In Finland it is 27. That is about 12 patients a year. [^care_curative] Compared with the best quarter of counties, 16.8 patients a year are missing (range 12.6–20.8). [^model] Compared with Finland as a whole, 7.2 fewer are operated and 4.9 fewer get radiotherapy that aims to cure. [^model] Patients in the OYS collaborative area do not wait longer: an estimated 31.2 days from diagnosis to treatment, against 36.9 in Finland. [^care_time_to_treatment] Fewer are treated to cure. [^care_curative] That is below the 24.6% that residents' age predicts. [^model] Some of the gap may be treatment that was given but not recorded. [^care_no_record]

## The target

Raise the share of lung cancer patients treated to cure from 18.5% to 22.2% by 2028: 5.2 more patients a year (range 0.0–7.7), for €211,500 a year, about €40,000 per extra patient. [^care_curative][^model] That closes 43% of the measured shortfall against Finland as a whole (12.1 patients a year). [^model]

## Funded actions

| # | Action and owner | Cost a year | More patients treated to cure a year (range) | First step this week | Measure: today → target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | **Step zero: fix the records (no direct effect)** | | | | |
| 0 | **Check the charts of patients with no treatment on record**[^ev_recording_audit_1]. Chief physician of oncology and the head of clinical coding | €8,000 | 0.0 | Pull 50 patients diagnosed in 2023 with no treatment on record and check their charts this month. | Share of patients with no treatment on record: 33.8% → 27.5% by 2027 |
| | **The county can start on Monday** | | | | |
| 1 | **Precise radiotherapy (SBRT) for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated**[^ev_sbrt_pathway_1]. Chief physician of oncology; chief of radiotherapy at the university hospital | €30,400 | 1.1 (0.0–2.3) | Write the referral rule: every stage I patient not accepted for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy the same week. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 18.5% → 19.3% by 2028 |
| 2 | **Travel and hotel paid for patients far from the university hospital**[^ev_travel_accommodation_support_1]. Chief physician of oncology and hospital social work; university hospital patient hotel | €43,600 | 0.7 (0.0–0.7) | Name one contact person who books the patient hotel and transport for every patient sent to the university hospital for curative treatment. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 18.5% → 19.0% by 2028 |
| 3 | **Fitness test and training before anyone is ruled too frail for curative treatment**[^ev_prehab_fitness_assessment_1]. Chief physician of pulmonology; leads of rehabilitation and geriatrics | €37,500 | 0.3 (0.0–0.3) | Decide that no stage I-III patient is recorded as "not fit" without an exercise test, and book the physiotherapy group. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 18.5% → 18.7% by 2028 |
| | **Needs the collaborative area (university hospital)** | | | | |
| 4 | **A chest surgeon reviews every decision not to operate**[^ev_surgeon_second_opinion_1]. Chief physician of pulmonology; chief of thoracic surgery at the university hospital | €41,000 | 1.7 (0.0–3.4) | Agree with the university hospital that a thoracic surgeon joins the weekly lung meeting, and send last quarter's stage I-II patients who were not operated for a second look. | Share of patients operated: 9.8% → 11.0% by 2028 |
| 5 | **Weekly video review of every stage I-III patient with the university hospital's specialists**[^ev_video_mdt_stage1_3_1]. Chief physician of pulmonology; lead of the university hospital lung MDT | €51,000 | 1.4 (0.0–1.6) | Ask the university hospital for a fixed weekly video slot and list every stage I-III patient diagnosed last month who was not discussed there. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 18.5% → 19.5% by 2028 |
| | **Total** | **€211,500** | **5.2 (0.0–7.7)** | | |

No trial has measured these effects; the low end of every range is zero. The ranges do not add up to the range of the total, because the measures share one ceiling. Costs are assumptions. [^model]

## Needs a national decision (outside this budget)

- **Low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers**[^ev_ldct_screening_1]: Ministry of Social Affairs and Health and Palko (decision), Finnish Cancer Registry (steering), county (delivery). €548,645 a year; modelled to avoid 0.9 deaths a year (0.2–2.4). Not counted in this budget. Not a county decision. Ask the Ministry and Palko for the timetable after the 2026-2028 pilot and offer the county as a pilot site. [^model]

## What to measure from Monday

- Share of patients treated to cure: 18.5% (2019–2023, measured) → 22.2% by 2028. [^care_curative][^model]
- Share of patients with no treatment on record: 33.8% → 27.5% by 2027. [^care_no_record][^model]
- Share of patients operated: 9.8% → 11.0% by 2028. [^care_surgery][^model]
- The registry's public figures cover 2019–2023; count these each month from the county's own records. [^care_curative]

## What more money buys, and what it cannot

The remaining €1.79M buys nothing more for this objective in the model, because the measures are limited by the reachable part of the shortfall, not by money. [^model] More would need a national decision on low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers, or ranking measures by deaths avoided instead. [^model] Lung cancer kills about 110 people a year in Lapland. [^deaths] This plan is modelled to avoid 0.8 of those deaths a year (range 0.0–2.3). [^deaths] [^model]

## Pilot ask

Six months with Lapland and its university hospital: ask what already runs, check 50 charts, then run the two actions that decide who is treated, for the part that is missing. In week 1, take the stored web-check questions to the university hospital. In weeks 1–8 spend €8,000 auditing 50 charts for stage, fitness, biomarker testing, why curative treatment was not given and where treatment happened. In months 3–6, run those two for what the hospital confirms is missing. Success is counted in charts audited, decisions reviewed, decisions changed and referrals made; patients moved are a secondary model estimate. [^model]

## Limits

- No trial has measured these effects; they are assumptions. Each range runs from all assumptions at their lowest to all at their highest, and is not a probability. [^model]
- The expected share is adjusted only for residents' age, not for stage, fitness, other illness, histology, how the cancer was found or smoking. County figures cannot show cause. [^model]
- 33.8% of patients have no treatment on record (Finland 27.5%). Audit the records before reading the gap as missing care. [^care_no_record]

pilot.comparison_en: Vantaa and Kerava is the comparison because it has Finland's highest recorded curative share (35.6%): a reachable level, not a causal control.
pilot.comparison_fi: Vantaa ja Kerava on vertailu, koska siellä kirjattu parantavan hoidon osuus on Suomen korkein (35,6 %): tavoiteltava taso, ei kausaalinen verrokki.
pilot.targets_en: Run the two actions that decide who is treated: a chest surgeon reviews every decision not to operate, and every patient who cannot be operated is referred for precise radiotherapy. The web check found both partly in place at the university hospital, so the pilot does only the part the hospital confirms is missing.
pilot.targets_fi: Tehdään ne kaksi toimea, jotka ratkaisevat, kuka saa parantavaa hoitoa: thoraxkirurgi arvioi jokaisen päätöksen jättää leikkaamatta, ja jokainen potilas, jota ei voida leikata, lähetetään täsmäsädehoidon arvioon. Verkkotarkistuksen mukaan molemmat ovat yliopistosairaalassa osittain käytössä, joten pilotissa tehdään vain se osa, jonka sairaala vahvistaa puuttuvan.
pilot.text_en: Six months with Lapland and its university hospital: ask what already runs, check 50 charts, then run the two actions that decide who is treated, for the part that is missing. pilot.text_fi: Kuusi kuukautta Lapin hyvinvointialueen ja sen yliopistosairaalan kanssa: kysytään, mikä on jo käytössä, tarkistetaan 50 potilaskertomusta ja tehdään kahdesta hoitopäätöksen ratkaisevasta toimesta se osa, joka puuttuu. Viikolla 1 viedään tallennetuista verkkotarkistuksista saadut kysymykset yliopistosairaalaan. Viikoilla 1–8 käytetään 8 000 euroa 50 potilaskertomuksen tarkistukseen: levinneisyysaste, toimintakyky, biomarkkerit, miksi parantavaa hoitoa ei annettu ja missä hoito annettiin. Kuukausina 3–6 tehdään näistä kahdesta se, minkä sairaala vahvistaa puuttuvan. Onnistuminen lasketaan tarkistetuista kertomuksista, arvioiduista päätöksistä, muuttuneista päätöksistä ja lähetteistä; potilassiirtymät ovat toissijainen malliarvio.

no_surgery_decisions_reviewed.basis_en: 64 patients are not operated in six months. Stage is not published by county; with Finland's stage mix (59% found at stage IV) about 22 of them have cancer that has not spread to other organs. Those are the decisions reviewed. The chart audit gives the county's own number.

pilot.cannot_show_en: 20.5% is the model's estimate for these two actions by 2028, not a measurement. The pilot is judged on the work counted, not on a promised change in the county's share.
